rows.what the ink shows: A descending p is followed by a small e loop, crossed x strokes and a separate final dot; the compact group is an abbreviation, with no extra ar letter bodies.

The pointed A, following u, projecting norm strokes and small lowered 2 are visible. The terminal relation is crossed by the thick deletion stroke; its surviving tips do not independently establish both strokes of an equals sign.

The opening sigma, rounded u/e remnants and two final norm strokes survive, but a large diagonal cancellation occupies the position where an initial A would have to be distinguished from the opening norm strokes.

The lower mark has a dark curled head and a continuous bent descending tail, with no detached dot. Its lack of the nearby numeral 2's bottom foot excludes that particular shape but does not positively establish a question mark; the punctuation identity remains uncertain.

An A apex projects above the cancellation, with its sloping left leg and straight right leg emerging below; short flanking norm strokes remain visible at the sides despite the heavy horizontal overstrike.

An oblique leg and short lower upright remain between the norm opening and the following u. Crossing cancellation strokes merge with the proposed apex and crossbar, so they do not establish a complete A independently.

A dotted initial remnant, a low middle curve and a long looped descender near the end project from the deletion line. Most letter bodies lie directly under that line, leaving the proposed words unverified.
At the start of the canceled sentence a short hooked s remains below the line, followed by a small i stroke with a clearly detached dot above it.

rows.reading: \unsure{est} fini, il \unsure{en est de même de}
rows.what the ink shows: After the covered first word, a long f stem, two dotted i positions separated by a low n, and a comma remain visible; the following il has a separate i dot and tall l. The later word bodies are mostly merged into the deletion line.
The canceled mark has the upper horizontal, descending diagonal and lower horizontal of a capital sigma; the horizontal deletion runs through its middle.
After the deleted sum, an upright and a curved diagonal tail survive below the horizontal cancellation, with a small separated dot to the right. They do not determine the intervening symbol or word.

A dotted initial and low rounded remnants remain at the place of the deleted abbreviation; the heavy horizontal cancellation merges the middle letters and ending. The full abbreviation cannot be distinguished from those remnants.
The initial loop and tall d stem are visible, followed by a low trace crossed by a dark stroke. The o/n/c bodies are not separately recoverable.
The dotted medial strokes and descending q lead into a compressed horizontal ending and a separated terminal t stroke. There is no written-out e-n-t sequence after the compact m ending.
Above the tensor circle, the hooked 2 has a separate short curved stroke on each side. Both parentheses are present, rather than a bare superscript 2.

Tall joined strokes at the left and two small dotted remnants near the right survive above and below the long cancellation. The intervening word bodies are absorbed by that line, so the complete proposed phrase remains uncertain.
The deleted word begins with a dot above dense ink and ends in low horizontal strokes with a detached small mark. Black overtracing hides the internal letter contours needed to confirm isom.

The short horizontal over E lies above its surviving upper arm and lower curved body; the separate long upper line spans E, tensor, and F, while cancellation runs obliquely across them. Above the tensor, a left curved flick and 2-like hook/right downcurl are crossed by deletion, so the raised (2) alone remains uncertain.
Two short tall stems rise from the erased body and a low initial trace enters from the left. The heavy blot masks the vowel bodies and final letter, leaving the whole deleted word uncertain.
A descending p, crossed t, dotted i, and two tall l strokes are followed directly by a long terminal stroke with a small t finish. No separate e-m-e-n sequence is written after the double l.
A small double-curved s is followed by a short i stroke and a separate raised dot; the cancellation crosses their baseline.
The first group retains a tall stem with a short shoulder; farther right only a small pointed rise and low traces survive between two cancellation lines. These do not establish the two deleted words.
A tall looped initial, isolated short uprights in the middle, and a final slanting crossed stroke remain, but the long cancellation absorbs the low letter bodies, especially the proposed sont.
The d has a distinct tall upright and left-hand bowl; the following e turns up and then loops below the horizontal cancellation.

The crossed sequence retains an initial ascender, several middle humps, and a later g-like descender followed by a tall upright. The bodies between these features are covered, so the complete proposed word sequence remains uncertain.

One tall looped f is followed by a low rounded a body, a short stroke with its own detached dot, and a crossed terminal t. The dot lies below the upper insertion and aligns with the deleted baseline; the clear space above the middle lacks the second tall f visible in same-page effet.
A large curved rising stroke and lower loop survive at the left; the following portion is a thick horizontal deletion with no independently distinguishable n shoulder.
The first group has a small loop and a terminal raised slash; a later upright projects above the line. The cancellation masks the connecting bodies needed to establish est de as a whole.

A low opening curve, a tall central stem with a lower turn, and a short terminal cluster remain beneath the insertion. Overlap and cancellation obscure the dotted first group and the central letter shoulder, so the full reading is retained as uncertain.
